one_month_reasoning: AppLovin's Q3 2026 report is not in the window: third-party calendars put it between Nov 4 and Nov 11, after the Oct 30/31 settlement (last year's Q3 came out Nov 5). The securities class action's lead-plaintiff deadline (Nov 16) is a procedural step and also falls outside. Events inside the window: (1) the FOMC on Oct 27-28, where Polymarket (Oct 1, $22M volume on the event) gives 74.5% to no change and 24.5% to a 25 bp hike. A hike would hurt high-beta growth stocks. (2) Late-October ad-platform earnings (Meta, Alphabet) as read-through on ad demand, plus any more sell-side channel checks like Edgewater's Sep 23 note or BofA's Jul 13 note, which each moved the stock 5-13% in a day. (3) A Polymarket market on the US-Iran ceasefire holding through Oct 31 is at 59.5%; a breakdown hit the stock in July. Short-horizon patterns pull against each other. The 12-month loser momentum effect and the persistent downward EPS revisions (19 down vs 5 up over 30 days) point lower. Short-term reversal after a 60% one-year fall, and a stock at its 52-week low trading at about 14x forward EPS while buybacks continue, point higher. With no scheduled company catalyst I stay close to neutral: a lognormal with a median of about $283 (a token reversal tilt) and sigma 0.20, close to the stock's usual monthly vol of 75%/3.5 = 21%.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (15x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of about $21.5, from a haircut 2027 consensus of $20.00, giving $322), FCF yield (2027E FCF/share of about $19.7 at a 6% required yield, giving $328) and EV/EBITDA (10x 2028E EBITDA of about $9.8B, giving $299). Weighted 40/35/25, this gives about $315 for a fair value 12 months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 of about $21.5 (2027E $18.5 after haircut, rolled forward with about 16% growth into 2028) x 15x

inputs_detail.value: $20.00 (27 analysts; was $21.16 60 days ago; 19 down / 5 up revisions in 30 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus cut by about 7.5% because revisions trend down and Edgewater's channel checks point to Q4 growth of only 8-9% q/q with MAX at capacity. About halfway between the consensus mean and the low estimate ($16.00).
$18.5 x 1.16. The consensus 2026 to 2027 EPS growth of 28% ($15.67 to $20.00) is halved for 2028 to reflect deceleration, which still includes buyback accretion of about 1% a year.

APP trades at about 14x 2027 consensus today ($281.31 / $20.00). The de-rated adtech peer TTD is at 14.2x. Meta bottomed near 9-10x in 2022 and re-rated to the low 20s. 15x is a small premium to TTD for growth above 25% and an 80%+ EBITDA margin, but below large-cap internet averages because of the regulatory overhang.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF of about $6.5B (rev $10.26B x 82% EBITDA margin minus about $1.7B cash tax and interest) / about 330M shares = $19.7 per share, at a 6% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 margin was 84% and Q3-26 guidance is 83%. I take 82% for mix and R&D growth (R&D more than doubled y/y in Q2).

H1-26 cash taxes were $640M on $2.94B of pre-tax income, with an effective book tax rate of about 16%. Interest is about $200M a year on $3.5B of debt. Scaled to 2027 pre-tax income of about $8B gives about 18% x $8B + $0.2B.
335.3M at 6/30/26, falling by about 3M a year from buybacks (H1-26 repurchases were $1.53B).
The NTM levered FCF yield is already about 6% (TIKR), up from about 2% at end-2025. I assume the market holds that de-rated yield rather than re-rating, consistent with a base case of no re-rating.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E EBITDA of about $9.8B x 10x = $98B EV, minus net debt of about $0.5B, / about 328M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: About 17% growth on 2027, a deceleration from the 27% implied by revenue consensus for 2027.
Long-term debt of $3.515B minus cash of $3.053B at 6/30/26.

The current EV is about $94.7B against 2027E EBITDA of about $8.4B, or about 11.3x. I assume a slight further compression on NTM as growth slows, in line with de-rated adtech (TTD at about 14x earnings).

bear.story: Edgewater's 'growth ceiling' turns out right: gaming wallet share is saturated, e-commerce self-serve ramps slowly, and 2027 growth falls to the teens. Meta and Google AI game and ad tools pressure share, the SEC data-practices probe or app-store/platform policy hits targeting, and EPS estimates fall toward $16. The multiple sinks to about 10-11x, like TTD's second down year (-68% in 2025, then -67% YTD 2026).

base.story: Growth decelerates from about 50% to the mid-20s in 2027 with margins about 82%. Buybacks continue, there is no regulatory resolution in either direction, and the multiple stays near today's 14-15x NTM EPS. The stock tracks earnings growth from a de-rated base, landing roughly flat to modestly up.

bull.story: The post-quarter AXON model upgrades and gen-AI creative tools show up in Q3/Q4 beats. E-commerce becomes a visible second engine (spend was already 28% above Q4-25 in Q2), revisions turn up, and the stock re-rates toward about 20-22x as with Meta 2023 (+194% after -64%) or APP 2023 (+~280% after -89% in 2022).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $190 the stock would trade at under 10x 2027 consensus EPS and about 8x EBITDA for a business guiding to 46-48% growth. That level only makes sense if earnings themselves are falling: a guide-down implying flat or negative q/q revenue, a material adverse SEC or platform (Apple/Google) action on data practices, or evidence that e-commerce and MAX share are shrinking. Ordinary 75%-vol noise around a $280-310 fair value would rarely push it that far without a fundamental break.

reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue was $1.924B (+53%), adj. EBITDA $1.614B (84%), EPS $3.76, 335.3M shares, net debt about $0.46B, and the Q3 guide is $2.055-2.085B. FY26 and FY27 consensus EPS are $15.67 and $20.00, with 2027 down from $21.16 60 days ago. At $281 the stock trades at 14x 2027 EPS with about a 6% FCF yield, so the 60% drawdown is mostly de-rating rather than an earnings collapse. The legs of the slide were: CapitalWatch short report, Google Genie and Meta iOS fears (H1); BofA's e-commerce note (Jul 13, -12.6%); the Q2 revenue miss and AI-model delay (Aug 6, -19.6%); Edgewater's 'growth ceiling' note (Sep 23); and Meta's Horizon tools plus the class action (late Sep). Base rates: Mauboussin's 6,500-stock study finds the median stock never regains its prior peak (54% never do) and takes about 2.5 years from trough to par, so a full recovery to $700+ in 12 months is a tail outcome (I put it at about 4.5%). Momentum literature and TTD's analog (a second straight year down about 67% despite still-growing revenue) argue for continued weakness while revisions are negative. On the other side, Meta 2023 (+194%) and APP's own 2023 (about +280% after -89%) show that profitable ad platforms at low-teens P/E can rebound violently once revisions turn. I weight these into a bear/base/bull of $170/$305/$470 at 30/45/25% (mean about $308). The ladder blends that scenario mixture with a single lognormal (median about $290, sigma 0.62, a bit below the 75% realized vol since part of it is event-driven). The result is P(>=$281) of about 53%, a median near $290, and a fair value of $315 from a P/E/FCF/EV-EBITDA blend. Limits: no option data was used, per the brief; Mauboussin's PDF and some sites returned 403, so the study figures come from secondary summaries; and there are no AppLovin-specific prediction markets on Polymarket or Manifold.
